question: In what year was the University of Lusaka (UNILUS) established?
answer: UNILUS was established in 2007.

question: What was UNILUS originally called?
answer: The University of Lusaka was originally called the Institute of Corporate Training and Applied Research (ICTAR).

question: When was the University of Lusaka officially opened?
answer: The University of Lusaka was officially opened on Thursday 18th October 2012 by Hon. Dr John N.T. Phiri.

question: What types of programmes does the University of Lusaka offer?
answer: The university offers Bachelor’s, Master’s, and Doctoral programmes, including its own programmes started in 2009 and earlier programmes offered in partnership with Copperbelt University.

question: Can I receive a master’s or doctoral degree for distinguished services?
answer: Yes. The University can award a master’s or doctoral degree to any person who has rendered distinguished services in arts, science, jurisprudence, or other branches of learning, or otherwise proven worthy of such an award, as stated in section 1.6.3.

question: Will every course listed in the handbook be offered to students?
answer: No. The University reserves the right not to offer a particular course, unit, or qualification even if it appears in the handbook, as noted in section 1.6.7.

question: How often do the university committees meet?
answer: All committees, including the Quality Assurance, Internship, Library and Fund Raising committees, meet twice a year and also convene on an as‑needed basis.

question: What are the main functions of the Internship Committee?
answer: The Internship Committee facilitates placements by providing institutional information to students, maintains a public web page with internship details, builds a contact database, manages the Mentorship Programme, and runs a monitoring programme to gather feedback from students and employers.

question: Who should I contact to obtain my transcript of records?
answer: According to the handbook, the Registrar is responsible for handling transcript of records.

question: How does UNILUS handle HIV/AIDS discrimination?
answer: UNILUS is strongly against discrimination on the basis of HIV status and embraces the spirit of Ubuntu in its fight against HIV/AIDS.

question: Does the University of Lusaka currently offer hostel accommodation for students?
answer: No. UNILUS does not currently have hostel accommodation. Students must arrange their own housing in nearby boarding houses. The university is planning student hotels in the upcoming main campus.

question: What are the steps to apply for a Bachelor's degree at UNILUS?
answer: Prospective students must: (a) obtain and fill an Application Form with qualifications and a passport‑size photo, paying the non‑refundable fee; (b) submit the completed form to the Registrar; (c) upon review, the university will issue a Letter of Admission indicating the formal registration date; (d) eligible applicants may apply for course exemptions; (e) after admission, students complete course registration before lectures commence.

question: When and how can I register for my courses?
answer: You can register online or in person at the university. Register at the start of each semester following the published enrolment timetable. If you miss the prescribed registration dates due to illness or exceptional circumstances, you may register late by presenting a medical certificate or other reasonable evidence.

question: What are the differences between full‑time, part‑time and distance learning students?
answer: Full‑time students attend day classes and carry the normal course load. Part‑time students attend evening classes with the same course load. Distance learning students receive a set number of assignments each semester, attend a residential school (2 weeks for undergraduates, 3 weeks for postgraduates), and also carry the normal course load.

question: What is the minimum lecture attendance percentage required for a student to satisfy the Senate’s attendance condition?
answer: A student must attend at least 80 % of the lectures delivered in the course to satisfy the attendance requirement.

question: After how many failed attempts at a course must a student seek Senate permission before they can re‑register?
answer: If a student has attempted a course twice and failed to obtain a pass, they cannot re‑register in that course without explicit permission from the Senate.

question: How do I register for an examination?
answer: To sit for an exam you must register with the Registrar for that specific course, paper or subject prior to the examination. This registration must be completed before the exam takes place.

question: What happens if I submit an assignment late?
answer: Two marks are deducted for each day an assignment is late, up to a maximum of seven days. An assignment submitted more than seven days after the deadline will not be accepted.

question: What is the procedure for applying to sit for a deferred examination at UNILUS?
answer: To apply for a deferred examination, a student must submit an application to the Dean of the concerned School no later than the last day of the semester examination session and before the start of the exam. The Dean will review the application; if approved, the student may sit for the deferred exam. The University Senate ultimately decides to grant the deferred exam. Note that missing an exam does not automatically entitle a student to a deferred exam and misreading the timetable is not a valid reason.

question: What are the CA percentage components for full‑time and distance‑learning programmes?
answer: For all degree programmes (full‑time and evening students): Mid‑semester exam 20%, assignments 10%, class tests 10%, final exam 60%. For distance learning programmes: two assignments (10% each, total 20%), residential class‑test session 20%, and final exam 60%.

question: What is the maximum duration of study for a four‑year degree programme at UNILUS?
answer: A candidate must complete a four‑year degree programme within six years. Years in which the student withdrew with permission are not counted toward the maximum period.

question: What does the 'Exclude School' comment indicate in a student's record?
answer: The 'Exclude School' comment is recorded by the Board of Examiners when a student has failed to meet the requirements of that school. The student will not be re‑admitted to the same school but may be considered for admission to another school.

question: What happens if a student receives a grade of F in a course?
answer: A grade of F is a fail and is awarded 0 points. Any course that receives an F (or a D) must be repeated when next offered.

question: What are the requirements for a student to proceed to the thesis stage in the MBA program?
answer: To proceed to the thesis stage a student must (a) have a cumulative GPA of at least 2.5 at the end of Stage 3, (b) submit the thesis to the Dean of the School within six months after completion of Stage 3, and (c) attend one of the two presentation periods a year. The thesis is examined by a committee of two examiners (one internal, one external) and graded on a 50‑point scale with a Pass/Fail outcome.

question: Under what circumstances will a student be excluded from the University?
answer: A student will be excluded if (i) they fail a course twice, (ii) they withdraw from their course of study without express permission of the Dean of the School of Graduate Studies, or (iii) they fail to meet the minimum GPA requirements and do not obtain a Pass in the thesis.

question: What is UNILUS’s stance on academic integrity and how should students report suspected dishonesty?
answer: UNILUS upholds a strict academic integrity policy that prohibits cheating, plagiarism, fabrication, and other dishonest acts. Students must report any suspected dishonesty to their lecturer immediately, providing evidence and a description of the circumstances. The lecturer will then decide whether to report the incident to the Registrar’s office for disciplinary action.

question: After detecting a suspected act of academic misconduct, how long does a lecturer have to notify the Registrar’s office, and what is the required initial notification to the student?
answer: Lecturers must inform the student within ten calendar days of detecting the incident. After notifying the student, they must report the incident to the Registrar’s office within fourteen calendar days of that student notification.

question: What are the two options a lecturer can choose when handling a suspected case of academic dishonesty, and what actions are involved in each option?
answer:
The lecturer can choose either Option A or Option B. 
• Option A – Discussion Agreement: the lecturer discusses the allegation with the student; if they agree on a sanction (e.g., grade reduction or additional work) no formal disciplinary action is taken, though a second or later offence may lead to further sanctions. The lecturer must indicate on the form whether agreement was reached.
• Option B – Academic Integrity Violation Report: the lecturer notifies the student, completes the violation report, attaches relevant materials, and forwards it to the Registrar’s office. Regardless of the option, the lecturer may assign a failing grade, adjust the course grade, or assign extra work, and any disciplinary sanctions are then decided by the Registrar.
